note: Static source analysis — browser not available in this environment. All measurements derived from exact className and DOM-structure reads of the source files.

root_causes.a_sideways_overflow: In SetupWizardPage.tsx the body wrapper is `<div className="flex gap-8">` with no flex-direction override for mobile. On viewports < 1024 px the second StepStrip renders its `lg:hidden` mobile bar as an inline flex-row sibling of the form card. Combined with `gap-8` (32 px), the two siblings share a fixed horizontal row whose combined min-content width exceeds the ~335 px phone viewport, pushing the right edge of the content past the right viewport boundary and clipping it.
root_causes.b_duplicate_stepper: `StepStrip` is called unconditionally TWICE in SetupWizardPage.tsx: once at line ~198 (outside the body flex, labelled 'step indicator') and once at line ~212 (inside the body flex, labelled 'desktop sidebar'). `StepStrip` returns a React Fragment containing both a `hidden lg:flex` desktop panel AND a `lg:hidden` mobile bar. On mobile both calls render the `lg:hidden` bar → two stacked progress strips. On desktop both calls render the `hidden lg:flex` sidebar → two side-by-side step lists.
root_causes.c_collapsed_card: Because `<div className="flex gap-8">` is a horizontal row on all breakpoints, the second StepStrip's `lg:hidden` div sits as a flex sibling of `<div className="flex-1 min-w-0">`. On a 335 px screen the stepper div takes its natural width (the row of 6 × 28 px circles + label text ≈ 230 px minimum) leaving only ~73 px of horizontal space for the flex-1 card. The card collapses to that width and word-wraps every character individually.
